nodes.label: Run Modes (Migrate / VerifyOnly / ProvisionOnly)
nodes.rationale: Three exclusive modes; options a mode would ignore are locked on the page with the reason, because showing them as available promised work that never happened. Verify only writes nothing at all; create-database-only opens the source anyway because a target named after a nonexistent source is a typo, not a plan, and a run that made the database but not the requested login is reported as failed.

nodes.label: Mirror Missing Tables Option
nodes.rationale: Creates tables the target lacks from the source schema — columns, NOT NULL, identity, primary and foreign keys — but not defaults, indexes or check constraints, so it is a fast stand-up, not a substitute for ORM migrations. It never creates an ORM history table and never mirrors rowversion, because a bytea NOT NULL column nothing can fill would make every application insert fail after a verified migration.

nodes.label: One User per Database Option
nodes.rationale: After a database migrates, a PostgreSQL login role with a 24-character random password is created from a {db}_user pattern and made owner of the database and its public schema. An existing role is reused and its password is not rotated, because something is probably already using it. CONNECT is revoked from PUBLIC only for databases this run created.
